correctness.rationale: A square-zero rank shell is exactly image/kernel flags with quotient-to-image isomorphism. Both images are uniform independent subspaces; after fixing their intersection the kernels extend independently by uniform Grassmann subspaces. Three standard explicit subspace-intersection counts yield the full rational joint law; all exponents, null boundaries, conditional ranks and sharp witnesses are proved. The d=1 Bernoulli reduction plus uniformly summable \(q^{-j(j+1)}\) Gaussian tails establishes the limit. The separately packaged exhaustive finite-field checker passes 111719 ordered pairs in 7 configurations including GF(4); finite checks corroborate, rather than replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The new complete joint law for opposite products of fixed-rank square-zero matrices and its dimension-sharp parity limit are not implied by the inspected existing counts of unrestricted mutually annihilating pairs (only the zero-zero event), bounded-nilpotent sum decompositions, or single random-matrix rank laws. Four actual semantic-index queries yielded no equivalent result among inspected hits, while independently known idempotent-product results concern a different matrix class. A broader representation-theoretic identity could still subsume this claim implicitly; this is expressly retained as priority risk.

value.rationale: The complete joint opposite-product-rank law is a naturally motivated invariant for two-generator index-two nilpotent matrix algebras, resolving information inaccessible from one-product rank marginals and zero-product counts. The sharp quantitative rigidity \(|\operatorname{rank}(EF)-\operatorname{rank}(FE)|\le\min(m,n-2m)\) contrasts exact equality in even dimension with a strictly positive limiting disagreement probability in adjacent odd dimensions. This structural dichotomy is an infinite-family result, not a routine small enumeration.
